- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — adjust downward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >80) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish — add 1–3% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently low (<0.3) over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–4 days — adjust forward by 0.5–1.5% per day for the next 3–5 days if sentiment is trending.
- Avoid over-optimistic peaks in late forecast windows (e.g., >85) — cap forecast at 85% of true peak or reduce by 2–4% if sentiment is cooling.
- If sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., >0.6) and price is rising, add 0.5–1% to forecast for next 3 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is falling sharply (e.g., <0.3) and price is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% to avoid overcorrection.
